samples.summary: Test titled "numbers an ordered list per indent level" uses a fixture with no indent levels, so the per-level counter logic is untested
samples.evidence:
The test at list-commands.test.ts:57-63 mounts `'a
b
c'` — three lines all at indent 0 — and asserts `'1. a
2. b
3. c'`. The behavior it claims to cover is `toggleKind`'s `counters = new Map<number, number>()` keyed by `p.indent.length` (list-commands.ts:222,231-232). With a flat fixture the map only ever has key `0`, so replacing the whole Map with a single `let n = 0` counter would leave this test green. No other test in the file toggles an ordered list over a nested/multi-indent selection (I grepped the file for `toggleOrderedList` — only two uses: this test and none with indentation; the indent/outdent block only uses bullets and a pre-existing `1. a
2. b`). The per-indent-level restart is new behavior shipped with a test that is presented as its coverage but cannot fail on it.

samples.summary: 'does nothing when the block cannot move' cannot fail: removing the guards it appears to cover leaves the document identical anyway
samples.evidence: list-commands.test.ts:183-189 mounts `'- a\n- b'` with the caret on line 1 and asserts the doc is unchanged after `indentList`/`outdentList`. Both compute `step === 0` (indentStep returns 0 because `itemAbove` is null; outdentStep returns 0 because `top.indent.length === 0`). If the `if (step > 0)` / `if (step < 0)` guards at list-commands.ts:268,274 were deleted, `shift(view, 0)` would rebuild the same prefix (`' '.repeat(0)`) and `replacePrefixes` would push no change — the assertion still passes. The test therefore documents the guards without exercising them.

samples.summary: Doc-unchanged assertions in the checkbox-input negative cases are vacuous — the `type()` helper never applies the default insert
samples.evidence: The `type()` helper (checkbox-input.test.ts:20-31) passes a `insert` fallback closure to each handler but never calls it when every handler returns false, so the document is never mutated on the negative path. Consequently `expect(view.state.doc.toString()).toBe('- [ ]')` (line 52) and `toBe('[ ]')` (line 66) hold no matter what the handler does short of dispatching — they would pass even if the real editor inserted the space. The meaningful assertion in each case is the `toBe(false)`; the doc assertion adds no signal and could mislead a later reader into thinking the typed space's normal insertion is covered.

samples.summary: No test asserts that `computeActiveFormats` now surfaces `list`/`canIndent`/`canOutdent` — the toolbar reads them from here, not from `computeListState`
samples.evidence: `computeActiveFormats` gained three fields (commands.ts:64,73-75) that `notes-toolbar.tsx` consumes for the five new controls. commands.test.ts only asserts `.bold`, `.italic`, `.link` (lines 58-73); grep for `computeActiveFormats` across packages/notes/src shows no assertion touching `.list`, `.canIndent` or `.canOutdent`. `computeListState` is well covered directly, but nothing proves the wiring into the object the toolbar actually receives.

samples.summary: The five new `NoteEditorAPI` list methods are exposed but never exercised through the API surface
samples.evidence: editor.ts:581-585 wires `toggleBulletList`/`toggleOrderedList`/`toggleTaskList`/`indentList`/`outdentList` onto the returned API. editor.test.ts's new test only covers the preview tick path; grep for `toggleBulletList` in packages/notes/src/view/editor.test.ts and in packages/frontend returns only the toolbar/detail source, no test. There is also no test for `notes-toolbar.tsx` at all (glob packages/frontend/src/app/notes/*test* returns only yorkie-note-store and notes-undo-integration), so a mis-wired button (e.g. Indent calling outdent) would ship green. Note the pre-existing `insert*` API methods are equally untested, so this is a continuation of an existing gap rather than a new one.

samples.summary: No test covers a task item nested inside another task item — the `clickedItem !== item` guard is only tested with a plain child
samples.evidence: preview.ts:281-282 rejects a click whose nearest `li` is not the resolved `.task-list-item`. preview.test.ts:182-195 exercises this with a *plain* nested bullet under a task. The complementary case — `- [ ] parent\n  - [ ] child`, where `closest('.task-list-item')` and `closest('li')` both resolve to the child and the toggle must report the child's own source line — has no test, so a wrong `data-source-line` on nested task items (the `note-task-source-line` core rule at preview.ts:58-68 iterates the flat token stream) would not be caught.

samples.summary: `itemAbove`'s blank-line skipping (loose lists) and `parentOf`'s stop-at-text rule are documented but untested
samples.evidence: list-commands.ts:123-143 deliberately skip blank lines when looking for the sibling/parent item ('a loose list keeps blank lines between its items') and stop at non-blank non-list text. No case in list-commands.test.ts puts a blank line between two list items before calling indent/outdent — the closest is 'skips blank lines inside the selection' (line 93), which only tests `targetLines`, not `itemAbove`. Removing the blank-line skip would leave the suite green.

samples.summary: `LIST_RE` accepts `*`, `+` and `1)` markers, none of which appear in any test
samples.evidence: The parser regex at list-commands.ts:32 is `/^(\s*)([-*+]|\d{1,9}[.)])(\s+)…/`. Every fixture in list-commands.test.ts uses `-` or `1.`. So `kindOf` classifying `*`/`+` as 'bullet' and `1)` as 'ordered' (list-commands.ts:57-61), and the toolbar's pressed state for a note written with those markers, are unverified.

list-commands.ts:294 returns without dispatching when the computed prefix equals the existing one (e.g. ticking an already-ticked box), which matters because every dispatch is a synced store edit. The setTaskChecked describe block (list-commands.test.ts:192-209) only flips values that change, and asserts on `doc.toString()` rather than on whether a transaction was dispatched, so a removal of this guard would be invisible.

verdict.reason:
Verified the fixture and the code under test. list-commands.test.ts:57-63 mounts 'a
b
c' (all indent 0) and asserts '1. a
2. b
3. c'; toggleKind at list-commands.ts:222,231-232 keys its counter Map by p.indent.length, so with a flat fixture only key 0 is ever used and a single scalar counter would yield byte-identical output — the test cannot fail on the per-indent-level restart its title advertises. Searched repo-wide for a counterexample: grep for OrderedList|orderedList yields exactly one test call site (list-commands.test.ts:60); the other notes ordered-list fixtures (list-commands.test.ts:66 converts an existing ordered list to bullets/tasks, :166-169 indents via shift() not toggleKind) never re-number across indent levels. Checked commands.test.ts (only computeListState for toolbar state), editor.test.ts, preview.test.ts, checkbox-input.test.ts, packages/frontend/src/app/notes/notes-undo-integration.test.ts and packages/backend/test/notes-cli-roundtrip.e2e-spec.ts — no indirect path exercises numbering. The documented behavior at list-commands.ts:217 ('numbered per indent level') therefore has no meaningful test, which is a missing-coverage defect in the test-adequacy lane.
